title: Audit plan received and council appointments reshuffled
subtitle: Staff awards, a new governance vice-chair role, and chair appointments for the Elliott committee of management.
overview: The committee opened by recognizing city staff for professional certifications and awards, including a national parking award, an environmental soil guidance award, a tourism marketing award, a culture days award and a national public works week award.

On audit, the committee received KPMG LLP's 2022 external audit plan for information {{vote:m1}}. The auditor described its approach, areas of focus such as post-employment benefits, contaminated sites, tangible capital assets and development charge reserve funds, and said it expects to report back in the spring.

On governance, the committee recommended several appointments through to November 15, 2024. Councillor Richardson would replace Councillor Busuttil as Vice-Chair of Audit {{vote:m2}}. The terms of reference would be updated to add a Governance vice-chair, with Councillor Busuttil appointed {{vote:m3}}. Councillor Downer would chair {{vote:m4}} and Councillor Klassen would be vice-chair {{vote:m5}} of the Committee of Management for the Elliott. These are recommendations that Council must still adopt.

decisions.detail: The committee received KPMG LLP's 2022 External Audit Plan for information.
The committee recommended that Councillor Richardson replace Councillor Busuttil as Vice-Chair of Audit for a term ending November 15, 2024.
The committee recommended updating its terms of reference to add a Governance vice-chair and appointing Councillor Busuttil to the role until November 15, 2024.
The committee recommended appointing Councillor Downer as chair of the Committee of Management for the Elliott for a term ending November 15, 2024.
The committee recommended appointing Councillor Klassen as vice-chair of the Committee of Management for the Elliott for a term ending November 15, 2024.

debate: The auditor explained that materiality was set at a level about midway in the allowed range of total revenues, and said a higher level would mean fewer transactions tested and less confidence in the conclusions. Setting it is the auditor's decision based on risk.
A councillor asked whether technology in audits reduces time and cost. The auditor said it has cut repetitive work and effort over time, but that higher quality requirements partly offset this.
A councillor asked about the effect of new auditing standards. The auditor estimated a modest increase in audit time and said staff may notice some extra work.

The auditor said development charges are an area of focus because revenue is recorded on a different timeline than cash is received. Spending from the reserve funds must also match the development charge study.

On governance, the Mayor said a Governance vice-chair would strengthen governance and provide backup for chairing. Moving the vice-chair of Audit to another councillor avoided one person holding two vice-chair roles, which would complicate the Elliott committee.
